subject: Session artifacts, residency options, and deletion timeline — quick Q&A
messages:
From: Jacob Reed <j.reed@olivehealth.com>

Date: 2027-05-27T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Question: what gets kept by default for streaming sessions vs final outputs?

Hi Mina,

Quick one from procurement/security as we finish the SOW review. We need a concise answer to two items so we can move to signatures: 1) For a typical hosted integration, what artifacts does Redwood retain by default for interactive/streaming sessions (partial tokens, intermediate fragments) vs the final generated outputs? 2) Can we require EU-only residency and get formal evidence that data was stored only in EU-controlled buckets?

We have some follow-up asks from our legal team (SOC2 evidence, deletion proof) — attaching the procurement checklist we shared earlier. Can you point us to what you retain by default and what customers can opt into/turn off?

Thanks,
Jacob
Procurement Lead, OliveHealth
(attachment: procurement_checklist.pdf)

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Jacob Reed <j.reed@olivehealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-27T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question: what gets kept by default for streaming sessions vs final outputs?

Hi Jacob — thanks for the checklist, that helps. Short answer up front, followed by a bit more detail and next steps:  

TL;DR: By default (hosted API): request inputs and final generated outputs are retained for 30 days for operational and quality-debugging purposes. Transient streaming fragments (partial tokens / in-flight fragments) are buffered for up to 7 days and then purged unless the session is explicitly captured as an archived transcript. Customers can request EU-only residency at contract time (we provide an EU region pin + export evidence). We’ll attach the retention matrix for the specific language your legal team will want.

Details:  
- Definitions we use:  
  * "Request inputs": the client payload (prompts, metadata) submitted as the API call.  
  * "Streaming fragments": in-memory/streamed segments emitted during generation before the final commit (used for debugging).  
  * "Final generated outputs": the final completion / message that the SDK/API returns (committed artifact).
- Default retention windows (hosted):  
  * Request inputs: 30 days 
  * Final generated outputs: 30 days 
  * Streaming fragments: 7 days (buffered for observability & replay debugging; not indexed)
- Opt-outs / controls:  
  * Customers can opt out of storing request inputs by enabling "no-store" on the API call or at tenant level (no-store means we never write inputs to persistent logs). 
  * Full EU residency: available as a deployment option (we provision resources in EU regions and restrict backups to EU-hosted storage).
  * Customer-managed KMS/HSM is supported for Private deployments (on-prem/VPC) — note that changes some evidence workflows.

Attachments: I’ve attached the retention_matrix_v3.xlsx with a row-level mapping to the procurement checklist. Kimberly, Marissa — adding you to cover SOC2/evidence + customer MRP (mutual action plan).

If you want a short one-page statement for legal, I can draft it and loop Kim for the final sign-off. Otherwise, we can run a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through the items.

— Mina
Senior Manager, Customer Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
(attachment: retention_matrix_v3.xlsx)

Subject: Fwd: Re: Question: what gets kept by default for streaming sessions vs final outputs?

Forwarding with some clarifications for the legal checklist and evidence. See inline notes below.

On 2027-05-27 at 11:18 Mina Haddad wrote: (message above)

Kimberly's notes:  
1) Evidence we can provide: 
   - SOC2 mapping doc (we can provide the control mappings used for retention/deletion).
   - Export of retention logs showing object timestamps + region tag (CSV extract) — useful for proof of EU-only residency.  
   - Erasure proof: when a customer requests deletion, we provide a signed deletion certificate with object ids and timestamps. That process is triggered via support ticket and audits are logged (ticket ID + timestamp).
2) On residency: 
   - EU-only residency is a contractual option for hosted customers. We pin the tenant to EU region, restrict replication and backups, and produce an export showing data locations. If OliveHealth wants permanent EU residency on hosted (no cross-border replication), we recommend a Dedicated/EU-reserved arrangement to remove shared-storage anti-patterns.
3) On streaming fragments: 
   - We treat streaming fragments as ephemeral telemetry; they are not part of the canonical customer data export unless explicitly captured. They are retained for up to 7 days to support replay debugging and quality investigations. If your security team requires zero buffering, that is achievable under Dedicated or Private where we disable the typical streaming buffer.
4) Evidence for deletion: 
   - Provide the SOC2 evidence bundle plus a post-deletion verification CSV and support ticket reference. For high-risk accounts we can arrange an independent attestation (additional fee/engagement).

If you’d like I can prepare a 1-page retention statement tailored to OliveHealth (language we can include in the SOW). Mina/Marissa — can you confirm the wording around 7-day buffer vs "never stored" API option so I can include exact claims?

— Kim
Director, Security & Privacy
Redwood Inference
(attachment: SOC2_evidence_request.pdf)
